class TestKillMutation341:
    def test_kill_mutation_341(self):
        # Create a timezone with a positive UTC offset
        tz = tzwin("GMT Standard Time")
        
        # Get the UTC offset for a date in the summer (when DST is active)
        summer_date = datetime(2020, 7, 1, 12, 0, 0)
        summer_offset = tz.utcoffset(summer_date)
        
        # Get the UTC offset for a date in the winter (when DST is not active)
        winter_date = datetime(2020, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0)
        winter_offset = tz.utcoffset(winter_date)
        
        # The offsets should be different (DST transition)
        assert summer_offset != winter_offset
        
        # Verify the offsets are correct for this timezone
        # GMT Standard Time is UTC+0 in winter, UTC+1 in summer
        assert winter_offset == timedelta(0)
        assert summer_offset == timedelta(hours=1)
        
        # Now test the fold behavior - this is what line 341 likely handles
        # Create a datetime that falls in the ambiguous period (fall back)
        # For 2020, DST ends on October 25 at 2:00 AM local time
        # So 1:30 AM on October 25, 2020 is ambiguous
        ambiguous_time = datetime(2020, 10, 25, 1, 30, 0)
        
        # The fold attribute should affect the UTC offset
        # fold=0 means first occurrence (before the transition)
        # fold=1 means second occurrence (after the transition)
        offset_fold0 = tz.utcoffset(ambiguous_time.replace(fold=0))
        offset_fold1 = tz.utcoffset(ambiguous_time.replace(fold=1))
        
        # These should be different because the fold determines which side of the transition
        assert offset_fold0 != offset_fold1
        
        # Verify the specific values
        # Before transition (fold=0): still in DST, so UTC+1
        assert offset_fold0 == timedelta(hours=1)
        # After transition (fold=1): back to standard time, so UTC+0
